raw_segments.text: Othello, it is the cause, it is the cause, my soul, let me not name it to you, you chase
It is the cause, yet I'll not shed her blood, nor scar that whiter skin of hers than snow,
Yet she must die, else she'll betray more men.
Put out the light, and then put out the light.
If I quench thee, thou flaming minister, I can again thy former light restore should
But once put out thy light, thou cunning'sty pattern of excelling nature, I know not where
is that promethean heat that can thy light relume.
When I have plucked thy rose, I cannot give it vital growth again, it must needs wither.
I'll smell it on the tree.
